And I mean that in the more traditional sense: give time to your neighbors and to organizations doing good work. | | | Feb 26 | | | | | | Given the writing I do in and around politics, for people I know socially, I've occasionally become their political therapist--what's actually worrying vs. what's just a sensationalist headline, etc. Needless to say, it has been a rough month. There is a lot to be worried about. In this informal, unremunerated role as a political therapist, the question I've been getting most: "What can I be doing?"1 Having thought about this a bunch, my answer: volunteer. And I don't mean volunteer by knocking on doors for political candidates--that has its time and place. I mean helping neighbors and volunteering for organizations that do good work. Why? 1. The most obvious: it's important and does good. If you are worried about the impact that our government is having, as I am, this is a pretty direct way to counteract that. This isn't resigning yourself to whatever is happening in Washington; to volunteer is to take a stand. 2. Volunteering makes you. In a political landscape where there isn't a lot to feel great about, it will literally make you feel better. 3. It's measurably . 4. In a moment where people feel lonelier and more disconnected than ever, it's a good way to build community and make friends. Information on how to volunteer is at the . The data on volunteering and charitable giving The Census Bureau and AmeriCorps, I was surprised to learn, track how often Americans over the age of 16 54% say they informally volunteer (at least once per year): helping a neighbor with groceries, offering free childcare, etc. 28% say they formally volunteer through an organization (at least once per year). It's been declining since then, and although it's , rates are roughly flat over the last eight years or so. Studies very consistently find that ,4 a finding that should give liberals pause--and encourage them to find ways to get involved and volunteer. Volunteering makes you happier, healthier, and live longer People are happier when they volunteer more; that's been reasonably well documented for a while now. The challenge, of course, is assessing causality: are people happier because they volunteer more? Or do they volunteer more because they're happier? It turns out that volunteering--causally!--makes you happier,5 according to a People who volunteer are also . The benefits extend to physical health too, and those who volunteer , were , have , and . Volunteering builds community and makes people less lonely Utah--which as I've written about, is a . On the flipside, . What's also notable about Nevada: , by far the lowest of any state.7 I've written about the before--it is one of the most pressing issues of our time.8 And it is no accident that , at least by one measure.9 Obviously, lower rates of volunteerism aren't the sole reason for that, but a lack of community--which ties into that lack of volunteerism--is a clear contributing factor. It turns out that who share your interests, values, and desire to do good. And sure enough, people who volunteer are : volunteers are 29% less likely to say that they're disconnected from their friends. Volunteering does matter This comes from a by : Last fall, a reader asked me what they could really do, as one person, to aid people living on the streets. "I often feel helpless to enact change," they wrote... My mind immediately went to systemic solutions, like voting for candidates who prioritize building more housing, or supporting efforts to loosen zoning codes. But when I called experts, their answers surprised me. Some of our ideas overlapped, but were ones I had admittedly not entertained: passing out socks or hand-warmers, donating items like sleeping bags to local shelters, or giving office supplies and bus passes to nonprofits serving unhoused people. Cohen's article--that for too many of us, charitable beliefs are a proper substitute for charitable giving and charitable deeds--is worth reading. I'm not saying that agitating for policy change is unimportant; it's very important. But giving back has an immediate and direct impact in a way that even good policy cannot. The say that volunteers improve the quality of their services and programs. Americans donate five billion hours of their time per year--the . It may not be enough, but that's pretty extraordinary. How to volunteer The simple answer: what are the causes you care about most? Reach out to those organizations; that survey I just mentioned (that found that most nonprofit leaders rely on volunteers) also . If you need help figuring out where to go, is a great place to start. Beyond that: For those of you in St. Louis, the is a good resource. I thought had two good threads too: and . For those of you elsewhere, reach out to local organizations you know and care about. has some good guidance. And as above, searching your city's local subreddit isn't a bad place to look either. I'll speak for myself: I used to volunteer more and then fell off during the pandemic. I'm , but at this point it's a flimsy excuse--the pandemic started five years ago now.11 There 's only so much I can do to change what's happening in national politics. But this is something that can make a difference and make all of us feel better about the world and our communities. I cannot think of a more worthy use of your time, or mine. Feel free to share this post with someone who will find this interesting. (If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, .) For press inquiries, please contact press@ben-samuels.com. 1 Often with an expletive thrown in there, I'll note. 2 The polling methodology was surprisingly difficult to track down. (I'll tell you why I cared so much about the methodology in a moment.) I went from to to a that directed me straight back to an where I found this footnote: "For methodological details, please see the full technical documentation and frequently asked questions about the CEV at data.americorps.gov." It all started feeling a little bit like : | | ---|---|--- But hey, the data must be in that FAQ...right? Nope. The AmeriCorps' data page doesn't even have an FAQ! Down the rabbit hole I went. Eventually, after way more searching than it warranted, I finally . (Note that opening this link will automatically download a 224-page document from AmeriCorps.) Why go through 45 minutes of trouble to find this? Because I was curious whether their data was observed or self-reported. Here's the answer, on p. 9: "The September 2023 Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement attempted to obtain self-responses from household members 16 years old and over." It matters that people self-reported because I think people likely inflate the amount of volunteering they do for the same reason we inflate to our dentists: it's the answer we know we should give, even if it's not totally true. There isn't any better data out there, but I bring all of this up to say: All of this data should probably be taken with a grain of salt. With that said, if questions are consistently asked over time, it's probably still a good measure of change. I've complained about government data before, and I'm sure I will again. With that said: the , I asked them to fix it and they did so within about 24 hours. So that was impressive and nice to see. 3 This data was first tracked, in earnest, going back to the '70s, so the spike in volunteering around 9/11 is the highest in at least the last 50 years or so. 4 Some of this, though not all of it, , and therefore how much people donate to religious causes (including tithing). But that doesn't account for everything. It should also be noted, : "We find that stronger religiosity increases volunteering toward individuals in their faith group (in-group). However, conservative beliefs reduce volunteering toward causes outside of an individual's faith community (out-group)." So it's not without its issues, clearly, but I'm comfortable nonetheless saying that more volunteering is better than less volunteering, even with these caveats. 5 There are different theories for why that is (one involving the ), but doing something good that makes you feel happier is a compelling combo. 6 More accurately, it finds that people who volunteer tend to be happier to begin with and become even happier when they volunteer. Even still, that's pretty cool. (h/t to The Washington Post for referring me to this study from .) 7 The New York Times ran an , but once again, pulling more recent data was surprisingly difficult--I had to manually work through a to get this. By the way, if you're curious: Louisiana has the highest percentage of its residents born in-state: 77%. 65% of Missourians were born in Missouri, the 14th-highest of any state in the country. * 57% of Americans were born in the state they live in today. So Nevada is way an outlier on all of this. 8 The percentage of people born in-state who live in-state is a highly inexact way of getting at whether someone has community or not. Lots of transplants build incredible communities, and of course lots of people who live in their hometowns are lonely. But it's one of the easier ways to look at this, and I don't necessarily think it's an accident that Nevada is at the bottom of both. 9 How you define loneliness is pretty challenging, so this is just one way of looking at it. Different people come to different conclusions by defining loneliness in different ways and weighting different measures. Some, of course, just make it up entirely. But the definition I used was backed by at least some data. 10 Just to be clear: this is about meeting friends, despite what Google thinks you have in mind when you're asking about meeting people while volunteering: | | ---|---|--- (By the way, if you're wondering, the internet seems to think... .) 11 Fourth graders at the beginning of the pandemic are in high school now. And that definitely makes me feel old... It's wild that it's been five years--it still messes with my sense of time. Ben Samuels is free today. | | **The NEGOP invites you to attend the 2025 Nebraska Republican Senators' Recognition Dinner** Dear Friends,
The **2025 Nebraska Republican Senators’ Recognition Dinner** , hosted by the Nebraska Republican Party**, **will take place on **March 27, 2025** , at the historic Lincoln Station in Lincoln, Nebraska.

The event, themed **"Nebraska: A Call to Greatness"** , will honor Nebraska's state elected officials, including State Senators, and recognize historical figures from the Nebraska Hall of Fame**, **such as John J. Pershing, Willa Cather**, **and Standing Bear**. **

**Our Keynote Speaker is former Congressman Jeff Fortenberry.** We anticipate attendance from our 33 Republican State Senators (looking for flexible committee hearing scheduling) and even further invites and recognition for our Governor, Constitutional Officers, Board of Education, UNL Regents, and other leaders within the Republican Party.

The theme of "Greatness" embodies the opportunities to coalesce on our shared values and as leaders from state-wide to local, striving to bring together from Governor to Municipality (Omaha & Lincoln) Candidates, to local school boards and counties - Panhandle to the River. This special evening provides an opportunity to celebrate Nebraska's leadership and history, while showing appreciation and support for those who serve the state.

| | Autism Health founders, Steve and Tracy Slepcevic, recently had the opportunity to join **Del Bigtree** on _The Highwire_ to discuss the urgent need for solutions in addressing autism and chronic illness. This impactful conversation highlighted the journey that led to the creation of the **Autism Health Summit** and the growing demand for alternative health solutions. This was more than just an interview, it was a powerful conversation about resilience, advocacy, and the urgent need for change in how to approach autism and chronic illness.

| At **Autism Health Inc.** , our mission is to **create awareness, empower families, and advocate for real health solutions** that address the root causes of autism. We are committed to **exposing the truth, connecting parents with life-changing resources, and building a strong, supportive community** that refuses to accept the status quo. To ensure that every family has access to the information and support they need, we offer **scholarships** for those facing financial hardship. If you or someone you know could benefit, **apply [HERE](https://autismhealth.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7c0b21e245e40197b3670bea2&id=43ba3f5fd9&e=3a42edfdc4) today. **

Join us at the **Autism Health Summit** on **April 11-13, 2025** , in **San Diego, CA** , where top experts will share groundbreaking research and innovative therapies. This life-changing event will bring together some of the **best doctors from around the world** , sharing their expertise on **underlying conditions, alternative treatments, and breakthrough solutions** for autism and chronic illnesses.

Together, we can create a healthier future for individuals with autism. We look forward to seeing you there!

body:
# [](https://act.robbonta.com/go/3?refcode=em20250226&t=1&akid=1665%2E1088799%2Eh_-47-)
Have you seen Rob in the headlines recently?
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-20250226?refcode=em20250226-1665&amount=5&refcode2=1665_1088799_h_-47-&akid=1665%2E1088799%2Eh_-47-)
First, **he was highlighted in the _Los Angeles Times_ for his decision to stay focused on his current role as Attorney General,** a job which is “powerful and ... meaningful on normal days. And in abnormal days, when you have a president who’s threatening democracy, the rule of law, and the Constitution, it’s very important.”
Rob explained how his work to hold Donald Trump accountable is personal: He remembers his father’s involvement in the civil rights movement and his parents’ experience living under a dictatorship in the Philippines until they moved to the U.S. and organized with labor leaders like Cesar Chavez. He is also concerned about the legal fate of same-sex marriages like his daughter’s under an administration that has been hostile to the LGBTQ+ community.
As Trump and his cabinet break the rule of law and attack our most basic rights, **Rob is leading the legal battle alongside other Democratic attorneys general, as highlighted in the _Washington Post._**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-20250226?refcode=em20250226-1665&amount=5&refcode2=1665_1088799_h_-47-&akid=1665%2E1088799%2Eh_-47-)
**[As the People’s Attorney of California, Rob is committed to fighting for the rights and well-being of ALL while defending our democracy. Voter Action Project
CFPM: Florida holds special primary election to fill vacancies in U.S. House
There are two big states holding special elections on April 1, Team. The state of Florida is holding a special election to fill vacancies in the U.S. House of Representatives, following cabinet nominations by President Donald Trump.
Why are these special elections important? Opponents of voting rights hold a 3 seat majority -- 218 to 215 -- in the House. One media report after another tells the tale -- Speaker Mike Johnson is having a hard time wrangling them all to vote for his priorities, and any dent made in that majority will make it harder for them to pass bills that harm voting rights this year or next.
It all starts with the American Confidence in Elections (ACE) Act which would nationalize voter suppression and the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, which would add onerous voter ID requirements, potentially disenfranchising millions of married women who changed their last names. Those bills are just the tip of the suppressive iceberg, with many in Congress looking to follow the election lies to policies that disenfranchise voters and make Trump happy.
We can stop all that with huge voter turnout in these Florida specials. But we need your help to make voters in Florida aware of these special elections, when early voting starts, how to request a new mail-in ballot, and so much more.

clean_body: Voter Action Project CFPM: Florida holds special primary election to fill vacancies in U.S. House There are two big states holding special elections on April 1, Team. The state of Florida is holding a special election to fill vacancies in the U.S. House of Representatives, following cabinet nominations by President Donald Trump. Why are these special elections important? Opponents of voting rights hold a 3 seat majority -- 218 to 215 -- in the House. One media report after another tells the tale -- Speaker Mike Johnson is having a hard time wrangling them all to vote for his priorities, and any dent made in that majority will make it harder for them to pass bills that harm voting rights this year or next. It all starts with the American Confidence in Elections (ACE) Act which would nationalize voter suppression and the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, which would add onerous voter ID requirements, potentially disenfranchising millions of married women who changed their last names. Those bills are just the tip of the suppressive iceberg, with many in Congress looking to follow the election lies to policies that disenfranchise voters and make Trump happy. We can stop all that with huge voter turnout in these Florida specials. But we need your help to make voters in Florida aware of these special elections, when early voting starts, how to request a new mail-in ballot, and so much more. The Trump administration has reinstated the Global Gag Rule, once again cutting off access to essential reproductive health care worldwide. This harmful policy forces organizations outside the U.S. that receive U.S. funding to choose between severely restricting abortion-related care and counseling or losing critical financial support.

In response, the Center for Reproductive Rights has relaunched its [**Global Gag Rule Pro Bono Clearinghouse**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102830865/530393821/-788023469?sourceid=1150454&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0201aaa-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTA3ODMyZS03NWY0LWVmMTEtOTBjYi0wMDIyNDgyYTk0ZjQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6mDTEL8ek0hk4jI7jM7TpiaV2-avbayeKvPcUVvlmvI=&emci=f728c826-75f4-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&emdi=1507832e-75f4-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ceid=954237), a legal support initiative mobilizing top law firms to help affected non-governmental organizations (NGOs) navigate compliance challenges and continue their critical and often lifesaving work.

We also want to ensure our supporters have the information they need to understand what's ahead—and how to take action. [**Join us for a special webinar**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102830866/530393822/733552186?sourceid=1150454&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0201aaa-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTA3ODMyZS03NWY0LWVmMTEtOTBjYi0wMDIyNDgyYTk0ZjQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6mDTEL8ek0hk4jI7jM7TpiaV2-avbayeKvPcUVvlmvI=&emci=f728c826-75f4-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&emdi=1507832e-75f4-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ceid=954237#/registration) on **Wednesday, March 5 at 2pm ET** , where **Mariakarla Nodarse Venancio, the Center's Global Advocacy Adviser** , will break down the policy's impact and what comes next. | [New York's Strengthened Shield Law Will Further Protect Doctors Prescribing Abortion Medication](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102830870/530393826/-1781766988?sourceid=1150454&utm_campaign=25emgfl-0201aaa-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTA3ODMyZS03NWY0LWVmMTEtOTBjYi0wMDIyNDgyYTk0ZjQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6mDTEL8ek0hk4jI7jM7TpiaV2-avbayeKvPcUVvlmvI=&emci=f728c826-75f4-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&emdi=1507832e-75f4-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ceid=954237)
---
With assistance from the Center for Reproductive Rights, **New York State has strengthened its telehealth shield law to further protect doctors prescribing abortion medication.** Under the new law, signed February 3 by Governor Kathy Hochul, providers prescribing abortion medication can request that a dispensing pharmacy print their practice’s name on the prescription bottle label instead of their name–making it more difficult for other states to target New York doctors.

Many people living in states with abortion bans or restrictions are unable to travel for abortion care, and telehealth has been a lifeline for those people. Shield laws protect abortion providers, helpers, and patient medical records when care is provided to out-of-state residents. **These laws are increasingly important under the anti-rights Trump administration that is emboldening state officials to prosecute doctors.**

The Center played a leading role in supporting shield laws across the U.S– these laws are currently on the books in 18 states and the District of Columbia. We pushed for these laws to protect not only doctors treating patients who travel from other states, but doctors providing care via telemedicine.

For every two steps forward, it feels like we take one step back. **But progress has been this nation’s hallmark —** because of the dreamers and innovators and organizers and activists who have never given up hope. I’m talking about people like you, Peter, and the champions of our democracy like the National Democratic Redistricting Committee (NDRC) who understand that our future is in our hands. **It depends on us, on the choices we make, particularly at certain inflection points in history — when so much is at stake. ** **[We are at such an inflection point right now. Since its founding eight years ago, I've been proud to support the NDRC and its Chairman, my friend Eric Holder. It’s because of this work that the last few election cycles have seen the fairest maps of my lifetime. It’s a big part of the reason we didn’t see a red wave in 2022, as some expected. And it’s why the margins in Congress are razor-thin today.
Think about this: Last year, the NDRC helped elect 116 of their endorsed Democracy Defender candidates — breaking a Republican supermajority in the Wisconsin State Senate, winning critical state supreme court elections in North Carolina and Michigan, and flipping key seats in state legislatures across the country. At moments like this, every single one of those victories is a step in the right direction.
**Our democracy is stronger today because of the NDRC — but our work together is far from complete, and more important than ever. **
Whether it’s increased attacks on the Census or extreme partisan gerrymandering, too many people are at risk of being deliberately left out of our democracy. And unlike the days when congressional and legislative districts were redrawn once a decade, these fights are now happening every year. _Yes, including 2025._
**There’s a lot of work to do in this moment and each of us has a role to play, which is why I need to ask directly: [Will you join me in supporting the NDRC’s work by making a donation right now?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102830913/530394141/-1665762292?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_PresidentObama_email_20250226-NDRC-Tier1-PresidentObama-NOR_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250226-NDRC-Tier1-PresidentObama-NOR_&utm_campaign=PresidentObama&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImFiZjgxZGUxLTczZjQtZWYxMS05MGNiLTAwMjI0ODJhOTRmNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=8jOzHYxhrRdukut1BWJbmq9CMDzKwLVxG8UskvfxBKw=)**

clean_body: This month, I have heard from many of my constituents who are fed up with the Republican Rip-Off. | | | | President Trump and his unvetted, unelected billionaire, Elon Musk, have been busy sowing chaos and confusion this month. President Trump is not focused on families and small businesses; he is solely focused on his extreme, out-of-touch agenda. This month, I have heard from many of my constituents – both here in person in Northwest Washington and via phone calls and emails – who are fed up with the Republican Rip-Off. I hear you, and I share your concern and frustration. The telephone town hall I hosted in February garnered strong attendance and engagement from the people of Northwest Washington, and that strong engagement is one of the tools we have to stand against this administration. When we push back against this Republican Rip-Off, we win. = Last week, I also hosted a roundtable with local healthcare leaders in Everett to discuss the impacts of Medicaid cuts on families in Northwest Washington. It is not pretend. Medicaid cuts will have real, negative impacts on moms, babies, seniors, children, and families. The stories I heard from the roundtable and the Northwest Washington community will help me make the case to folks in Congress that they ought to care. The negative impact we feel from this administration is also felt throughout the country. In my role as a ranking member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, I visited Los Angeles to get a better understanding of what other areas are experiencing. Alongside fellow Transportation & Infrastructure Committee members Congresswoman Laura Friedman and Congressman Robert Garcia, we met with community leaders and key stakeholders across Los Angeles to better understand how budget concerns will impact critical infrastructure projects. One of the projects at risk is the Los Angeles River Restoration Project which aims to revive 11 miles of the river. Along with critical projects at home like Skagit transit maintenance, improving rail safety and reducing congestion in Everett, and local sustainability efforts in Northwest Washington — people are feeling the pain of the Republican Rip Off across the country. This administration wants to illegally cut funding to important projects like the Los Angeles River Restoration Project — all so they can instead give a $4.5 trillion tax cut for the richest Americans and wealthiest corporations, just as they did in 2017. I know the road ahead under this new administration seems daunting — but we still can stand up for our communities and win. Continue to be engaged, and speak out when you or your community is hurting. Together, we can take a stand against the Republican Rip-Off. "**First measles death in West Texas reported by Texas Tech hospital,** " Houston Chronicle's**Catherine Dominguez** and**Evan MacDonald** -- "A child died from the measles after being hospitalized in Lubbock, the first death [amid an outbreak that began last month in the South Plains region](https://substack.com/redirect/1e63ec9b-f037-4be6-9655-89b98fb164d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), health officials said.

The Texas Department of State Health Services confirmed the school-aged child's death on Wednesday but did not offer any additional details about the child's age or identity. The child had not received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella before being hospitalized last week, department officials said.

The [measles outbreak in northwest Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/b6473c1c-f681-4f50-89db-bb049addcb7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) grew to 124 cases in nine counties on Tuesday, and health officials warned that residents in other parts of the state may have been exposed to the highly contagious respiratory illness.

The [state's largest measles outbreak in more than 30 years](https://substack.com/redirect/1e63ec9b-f037-4be6-9655-89b98fb164d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has already spread to neighboring New Mexico, which reported nine cases on Tuesday. The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services now includes a handful of cases in the northernmost part of the Panhandle and potential exposures in San Antonio and San Marcos.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/924344f8-3ae6-4132-9d4a-511a5c7bf647?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The outbreak is still concentrated in school-aged children, who account for 101 of the 124 cases. Only five of the cases are individuals who have received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella; the rest are those who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.

Measles is spread through coughing and sneezing and can linger in the air for up to two hours. It's also highly contagious; up to nine in 10 people who are exposed to the virus will become infected if they aren't vaccinated, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

It can also lead to serious health complications. One in five unvaccinated people who are infected will need to be hospitalized, and one in 20 children will develop pneumonia, according to the CDC. In rare cases it can lead to brain swelling, blindness and death.

Health officials have stressed that two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles, and vaccinated individuals generally experience milder symptoms if they do become sick, according to the CDC. Measles can cause serious illness; 18 people have been hospitalized amid the current outbreak in northwest Texas, according to the DSHS.

"For those who are not vaccinated against the measles, now is the time," Dr. **Ericka Brown** , local health authority for Harris County Public Health, said during a Tuesday news briefing. "That really is the best method of prevention."" TOP NEWS "First measles death in West Texas reported by Texas Tech hospital, " Houston Chronicle'sCatherine Dominguez andEvan MacDonald -- "A child died from the measles after being hospitalized in Lubbock, the first death , health officials said. The Texas Department of State Health Services confirmed the school-aged child's death on Wednesday but did not offer any additional details about the child's age or identity. The child had not received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella before being hospitalized last week, department officials said. The grew to 124 cases in nine counties on Tuesday, and health officials warned that residents in other parts of the state may have been exposed to the highly contagious respiratory illness. The has already spread to neighboring New Mexico, which reported nine cases on Tuesday. The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services now includes a handful of cases in the northernmost part of the Panhandle and potential exposures in San Antonio and San Marcos. The outbreak is still concentrated in school-aged children, who account for 101 of the 124 cases. Only five of the cases are individuals who have received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella; the rest are those who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. Measles is spread through coughing and sneezing and can linger in the air for up to two hours. It's also highly contagious; up to nine in 10 people who are exposed to the virus will become infected if they aren't vaccinated, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It can also lead to serious health complications. One in five unvaccinated people who are infected will need to be hospitalized, and one in 20 children will develop pneumonia, according to the CDC. In rare cases it can lead to brain swelling, blindness and death. Health officials have stressed that two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles, and vaccinated individuals generally experience milder symptoms if they do become sick, according to the CDC. Measles can cause serious illness; 18 people have been hospitalized amid the current outbreak in northwest Texas, according to the DSHS. "For those who are not vaccinated against the measles, now is the time," Dr. Ericka Brown , local health authority for Harris County Public Health, said during a Tuesday news briefing. "That really is the best method of prevention."" ($) FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. The grew to 124 cases in nine counties on Tuesday, and health officials warned that residents in other parts of the state may have been exposed to the highly contagious respiratory illness. The has already spread to neighboring New Mexico, which reported nine cases on Tuesday. The latest update from the Texas Department of State Health Services now includes a handful of cases in the northernmost part of the Panhandle and potential exposures in San Antonio and San Marcos. » The outbreak is still concentrated in school-aged children, who account for 101 of the 124 cases. Only five of the cases are individuals who have received the vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella; the rest are those who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. Measles is spread through coughing and sneezing and can linger in the air for up to two hours. It’s also highly contagious; up to nine in 10 people who are exposed to the virus will become infected if they aren’t vaccinated, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It can also lead to serious health complications. One in five unvaccinated people who are infected will need to be hospitalized, and one in 20 children will develop pneumonia, according to the CDC. In rare cases it can lead to brain swelling, blindness and death. » Health officials have stressed that two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles, and vaccinated individuals generally experience milder symptoms if they do become sick, according to the CDC. Measles can cause serious illness; 18 people have been hospitalized amid the current outbreak in northwest Texas, according to the DSHS. “For those who are not vaccinated against the measles, now is the time,” Dr. Ericka Brown , local health authority for Harris County Public Health, said during a Tuesday news briefing. “That really is the best method of prevention.”" ($) | FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. Team,

Look, I know how difficult it is to keep up with Trump’s never-ending news cycle.

To constantly hear about the damage and destruction, and the pain and suffering, caused by Trump and his people.

To read about our country embarrassing itself, yet again, on the international stage.

And then to listen to the same tired reactions from our elected leaders who, like clockwork, express “ _concern_ ” about the utter insanity that is happening right before our eyes.

These are the people who _can_ actually DO something. These are the folks who have been _given power by the people_ to push back and ACT in OUR best interest.

And I know that it can sometimes feel hopeless and frustrating. But—we also have power. **And we also must act to make our voices heard.**

I am running for Congress to rally the nation to our cause. Flipping this open seat from red to blue sends a powerful message to every do-nothing member of Congress and every Democrat who is afraid to stand up and fight: **_we are fed up with your inaction and DEMAND more._**

I am running on a platform for all the people and for the working class: Medicare for All, strong unions, affordable housing, and lowering prices. Our message is resonating with voters across both parties.

| | Hi there, Republicans just passed a budget plan that slashes Medicaid, cuts food assistance for seniors, and guts services for children with disabilities — all while adding $3 trillion to the national debt. Why? To give massive tax breaks to billionaires like Elon Musk. On top of that, Musk's so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) has already hit close to home. **Thirteen workers at Lake Mead National Recreation Area were fired, including one responsible for monitoring toxic water levels.** This reckless move doesn't just endanger employees — it puts visitors and families at risk by threatening the safety of our public spaces. Worse still, these cuts do absolutely nothing to lower gas prices, reduce grocery costs, or make housing more affordable. I’m doing what I can to push back and make it clear that these senseless cuts are wrong for the hardworking families in this country. But I need your help. Your donations are more than just numbers on a screen — they’re fueling the next phase of our campaign by:
* **Expanding our voter outreach** — funding phone banks, canvassing tools, and digital ads that connect us with key swing voters.
* **Hiring crucial staff** — field organizers, communications specialists, and campaign strategists who ensure our campaign stays on track and responsive.
* **Hosting community events** — bringing our message directly to voters, listening to their concerns, and rallying support for a better future.

name: Tobias Read
subject: Standing up for our democracy has never been so important
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250226em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250226em]
Hi folks, it’s Tobias Read.
Around the country, our elections are under attack:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250226em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250226em]
There are some (in this case, the RNC) that are doing everything they can to make it harder for regular people to cast their vote, even if that ends up silencing and disenfranchising some voters.
It is counter to everything that is in the best interest of voters and our democracy.
As Secretary of State, I am responsible for ensuring that our elections are conducted securely, democratically, and fairly.
One way we can do that is by making Vote-by-Mail easy and reliable. Until recently, Oregon’s vote-by-mail system was supported by a broad cross-section of Oregonians. But now, some Republicans have decided to attack It, even here in Oregon.
These opponents constantly claim rampant voter fraud as justification for implementing restrictive anti-democracy election laws, but I’m here to tell you that voter fraud is not the issue.
Voter disenfranchisement is.
Vote By Mail is a secure way to make voting more accessible, and my office works daily to protect this essential right. However, I think it’s more accurate to talk about Vote at Home. You can deliver your ballot by mail, return it to a drop box, or take it to your county clerk’s office.
Please contribute whatever you can today to support my work, spread my message, and join me in the fight to protect our elections. Any amount will make a big difference, but most donors give $30.50. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250226em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250226em]
Thank you for your help.
Tobias Read
P.S. Don’t forget! The Oregon Political Tax Credit allows you to donate $50 (if you file single) or $100 (if you file joint) to a candidate, PAC, or party, which will be fully credited back as a rebate — so it’s free to donate! For more information, click here. [https://www.oregon.gov/omd/ONG/Documents/SMFS/Personal%20Financial%20Counselor/Political-Tax-Credit.pdf?]

Peter,

I recently introduced a bill in the U.S. Senate that would finally declare English as the official language of the United States.

It’s just common sense–but the radical left had a _meltdown_ , calling me a racist and a bigot.

But as one of the only naturalized citizens serving in the U.S. Senate, **I am here to tell you Americans don’t have to be ashamed of our culture.**

When I moved here legally with my family from Colombia at age five, I didn’t speak a word of English.

But I was determined to master the language because it was clear to me that this was the whole reason my family came here— _to become Americans._

**The proudest moment of my life was becoming an American citizen at age 18, a process that showed me just how foundational the English language is to the American way of life.**

It’s long past time that we enshrine this simple fact into law.

clean_body: It’s long past time that we enshrine this simple fact into law. | Peter, I recently introduced a bill in the U.S. Senate that would finally declare English as the official language of the United States. It’s just common sense–but the radical left had a meltdown , calling me a racist and a bigot. But as one of the only naturalized citizens serving in the U.S. Senate, I am here to tell you Americans don’t have to be ashamed of our culture. When I moved here legally with my family from Colombia at age five, I didn’t speak a word of English. But I was determined to master the language because it was clear to me that this was the whole reason my family came here— to become Americans. The proudest moment of my life was becoming an American citizen at age 18, a process that showed me just how foundational the English language is to the American way of life. It’s long past time that we enshrine this simple fact into law. Please weigh in as the Senate debates this issue. Thank you! subject: The truth about the GOP’s attacks on me.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
They want the focus to be on their theatrics so that it won’t be on the issues I laid out in my speech.
Hi Peter, it’s Congresswoman Sarah McBride — Heartland Patriots said I could reach out to you about something important.
You may have heard that I recently gave my first speech as Delaware’s Congresswoman on the floor of the House of Representatives. And you may have also heard that the Republican who recognized me when I came to the podium used the moment to refer to me as the “Gentleman” from Delaware, “Mr. McBride.” A thoroughly unoriginal schoolyard taunt against trans people.
In truth, they want the focus to be on their theatrics so that it _won’t_ be on the issues I laid out in my speech: the MAGA effort to gut our government at the expense of working people and my focus on bringing down costs and building a government that respects everyone.
Really, their attacks are about more than just me. The truth is they are using trans people as a pawn in their scheme to gut the federal government and line the pockets of Donald Trump’s best friends.
**But I refuse to be a pawn. I refuse to give them that power. And I refuse to let them get away with it.**
That’s why I’m going to spend every day fighting _against_ their attempts to dismantle the federal government, and fighting _for_ the things Delawareans elected me for — regardless of what kind of personal insults Republicans want to throw my way.
Republicans know what they’re doing right now is unpopular, and that’s why they’re desperate to change the conversation. It’s up to us to make sure they don’t get away with it.
**[Peter, if you’re with me, Heartland Patriots and I could really use your support at this moment. name: State Representative Ryan Chamberlin
subject: Newsletter from Rep. Ryan Chamberlin
body:
Newsletter from Rep. Ryan Chamberlin | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/newsletter-from-rep-ryan-chamberlin-12725550?e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| |
---
| | **NEWSLETTER FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN**
---
| Friends and Neighbors,

Last week, we wrapped up our final week of committee meetings before the legislative session kicks off at the beginning of March. Over the last several weeks, my fellow legislators and I have been hard at work for our individual communities and state, and we are ready to continue the fight for our constituents in Tallahassee very soon. I look forward to being a champion for the issues that matter most to Floridians, like property tax relief and public safety, during this upcoming session. Together, we can keep our state the Free State of Florida and build a better and brighter future for the next generation.

As always, my office is here to serve you! Please do not hesitate to [contact my team](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=398e672282&e=d1c1b9864f) if you need assistance with anything. We would be happy to help in any way we can!
---
|
---
| | **Monday, February 10 - Florida Chamber of Commerce Annual Bills, Beers, & Business Legislative Reception**
---
|
---
---
| I had the pleasure of attending the Florida Chamber of Commerce Annual Bills, Beers, & Business Legislative Reception. It was great to join fellow elected officials and leaders in business to learn more about the issues important to our Florida business community.
---
| | **Tuesday, February 11 - Special Session, Meetings, & Receptions in Tallahassee**
---
| I began the day with Special Session, where we championed President Donald Trump’s America-First agenda to secure our border, crack down on illegal immigration, and keep our communities safe.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with representatives from the Ocala/Marion County Chamber & Economic Partnership._
| I then had a meeting with the Ocala/Marion County Chamber & Economic Partnership to discuss appropriation projects for this upcoming legislative session.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with Emily Ogden and another team member from CSL Plasma._
| I also had the opportunity to meet with CSL Plasma, who have facilities in our district back home. It was a pleasure to meet Emily Ogden and discuss their legislative priorities for this upcoming session and to learn more about the company.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with Americans for Prosperity._
| I enjoyed a great visit from Americans for Prosperity during their day on the hill to discuss legislative priorities. It was great to meet with constituents and individuals from all around the state.

My day concluded with receptions that were attended either by me or my wonderful staff. I was honored to be represented at the Florida Behavioral Health BBQ, the Stetson DATC Reception, and the Florida Mental Health Advocacy Coalition Reception.
---
| | **Wednesday, February 12 - Additional Meetings & Receptions in Tallahassee**
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with SMA Healthcare VP Salvatore Gintoli._
| I started off a busy day meeting with SMA Healthcare VP Salvatore Gintoli to discuss their operations and appropriation requests for this upcoming legislative session.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with a representative from the Ocala/Marion Community Foundation._
| I then had the opportunity to meet with the Ocala/Marion Community Foundation to discuss their projects in the district, legislative priorities, and appropriations.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with Jason Kasten from the Arnette House._
| It was great to meet with Jason Kasten from the Arnette House. He stopped by my office to discuss the children in their care and their services.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with members of the Marion County School Board._
| I had the pleasure of meeting with the Marion County School Board to discuss legislative priorities and appropriations. They also gave me an update on what they have been working on for our schools back in the district.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin presenting HB 113._
| I then had the opportunity to present my bill, [HB 113 - Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Law Enforcement Officer](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=5d350f5e88&e=d1c1b9864f), to the Criminal Justice Subcommittee, which passed favorably.
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with representatives from the Florida American Waterworks Association._
| To end the day, I met with the Florida American Waterworks Association to discuss their legislative priorities.

I also attended receptions for the Florida American Waterworks Association, Epilepsy Alliance, as well as the Florida Pharmacy Networking Social.
---
| | **Thursday, February 13 - Committee Meetings & Special Session**
---
| I began my day sitting on the Human Services Subcommittee and ended it on a high note with Special Session, where we passed the strongest legislation in the nation to combat illegal immigration. Learn more about this legislation by clicking [here](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=221e4c2826&e=d1c1b9864f) and [here](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=03af517a12&e=d1c1b9864f).
---
| | **Tuesday, February 18 - More Meetings & Receptions in Tallahassee**
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with Kids Central CEO John Cooper._
| I started my morning with a meeting with John Cooper, CEO of Kids Central. We discussed their legislative priorities and the child welfare program in Florida.
---
| I then had the opportunity to meet with Family Support Services to discuss the great work they are doing in Florida and upcoming child welfare legislation. I also had a meeting with the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers to discuss their legislative priorities for this year.

To end the day, I sat on the Justice Budget Subcommittee and attended receptions for Wild FL and United Way.
---
| | **Wednesday, February 19 - Speaking Engagements & Committee Meetings**
---
|
---
---
| I had the privilege of speaking to the members of the FL Coalition for Children on my bill, [HB 415 - Community Based Care Lead Agency and Subcontractor Liability](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=e197a01698&e=d1c1b9864f). Senator Stan McClain and I shared our stories and then answered some questions from the members.

I then had a meeting with the Florida Airports Council. They represent 129 public airports, which play a role in Florida’s $300 billion aviation industry. To end the day, I sat on the Intergovernmental Subcommittee and the Human Services Subcommittee. I also attended receptions for Foley & Lardner LLP, the Florida Nurses Association, and the Florida Airports Council.
---
| | **Thursday, February 20 - Meetings in Tallahassee**
---
|
---
_Rep. Chamberlin with representatives from Grace Christian School of Ocala._
| I started the day sitting on the Economic Infrastructure Subcommittee and then enjoyed a productive meeting with Grace Christian School of Ocala.
---
| | **Florida House of Representatives: Week in Review**
---
| We have had a productive several weeks in Tallahassee, and I want to ensure the district stays informed and knows that the Florida House is working hard for all Floridians. Please click **[here](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=273950d444&e=d1c1b9864f)** to read the Florida House’s Week in Review newsletter from the week of February 10 and **[here](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=c787b8366b&e=d1c1b9864f)** to read the latest edition from last week.
---
|
---
| | Thank you for reading, and I look forward to sharing with you again soon.

Have a great rest of your week!

Best regards,

**Ryan Chamberlin**
******State Representative**
**District 24**
---

Peter,
This morning, news broke that Jeff Bezos forced out _The Washington Post’s_ Opinion Editor, aligning its editorial direction more closely with a right-wing agenda.
In an email to staff, Bezos announced that the Opinion section will now focus exclusively on "free markets" and "personal liberties." He added that dissenting views will no longer be allowed.
**The opinion page changes are the latest blow to _The Washington Post’s_ journalistic independence. Bezos—whose company Amazon receives billions in government contracts—is now more focused on currying favor with Donald Trump than preserving _The Post’s_ history as a vital defender of American democracy.**
[**We’ll explain more in a moment. But if you value fearless, independent journalism that isn't afraid to hold Trump accountable, chip in $25 today to help COURIER fight back.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/102837938/530413742/1026506809?refcode=20250226_wapo_opinion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTUyZTQwYTgtODJmNC1lZjExLTkwY2ItMDAyMjQ4MmE5NGY0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3mMXtq56sklqZd6dseQz2x24F2Mw8H8BJyH759j8qQM=)

Bezos claims these changes are just an “editorial shift.” In reality, they are another abdication of duty for what was once a vital American institution.
**David Shipley, the Opinion Editor Bezos forced out, was the same editor who resisted Bezos’ decision to block _The Post_ from endorsing Kamala Harris last year. This was the first time in 40 years that the paper had declined to endorse a candidate.**
Shipley also backed Pulitzer Prize-winning cartoonist Ann Telnaes, who resigned in protest after _The Post_ killed her cartoon depicting Bezos and other billionaire media owners kneeling at Trump’s feet and handing over bags of money.

**[SEE THE CARTOON & DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/102837941/530413772/1026506809?refcode=20250226_wapo_opinion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTUyZTQwYTgtODJmNC1lZjExLTkwY2ItMDAyMjQ4MmE5NGY0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3mMXtq56sklqZd6dseQz2x24F2Mw8H8BJyH759j8qQM=)**
The _Washington Post_ is the newspaper that took down Nixon, exposed Watergate, and set the gold standard for investigative reporting.
**Now, as Trump and Elon Musk usher in an unprecedented era of government corruption, Bezos is signaling that _The Post_ is yet another captured corporate media outlet – all to protect its owner’s bottom line.**
That’s why your support for COURIER and our mission is so urgent right now. If we want real journalism that won’t bow to Trump or a fear of losing profits, we have to build it ourselves, and that's exactly what we're doing with your support.

Their latest ploy? The mass firing of veterans who are serving in the federal government, without just cause. To be blunt: It’s appalling, atrocious, and downright unpatriotic.

Team,

On Monday night, we had our ninth annual IDCCA Party Builder Awards Reception, where we honored four incredible people who have dedicated their lives to helping build the Democratic Party in Illinois and throughout the United States.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2025partybuilderawards?refcode=IDCCA_EMAIL_260225_NA_TY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2025partybuilderawards?refcode=IDCCA_EMAIL_260225_NA_TY] Photo Credit: Mark Lind
This was our largest ever Party Builder Awards Reception. It was a well deserved and earned spotlight as we honored Ben Head (Co-Founder of Operation Swing State), Congresswoman Robin Kelly (IL 2nd), attorney Joe Power (Founding Partner of Power Rogers Trial Lawyers), and State Senator Ram Villivalam (8th District / 38th Ward Democratic Committeeperson).

This event is one of our most important every year. It is our chance to thank those who have given tirelessly to the Democratic Party. We couldn’t be prouder of this year’s honorees and we are thankful to count them as our friends.

If you attended, bought tickets, made a donation, or read our emails about the event – thank you! We’re only able to do events like this and connect with our community because of the support of people like you.

Thank you for everything – and now let’s get back in the fight to save our country from Trump and Musk.

Best,
Mark Guethle
IDCCA President

| RUNNING FOR GOVERNOR RUMORS
---
|
# AMANDA CHASE
---
|
# VIRGINIA'S HONEY BADGER
---
| Dear Hello I'm absolutely humbled by the number of you who have contacted me to run for Governor. The unsolicited response has been overwhelming to the point I've decided to respond.
First, I had no intentions of running for Governor this year. My thought was that we get behind our one Republican nominee who has declared, so that we don't have to waste time or money in a Republican Primary, so that we can laser focus all of our resources on defeating Democrat Governor hopeful Abigail Spanberger.
In the past few days, I've learned that our only declared Republican candidate for Governor has encountered some pretty serious issues with her campaign.
We now face an almost certain defeat in November, if we don't find a candidate who can manage and organize a successful campaign against Spanberger.
Many in Southwest Virginia have said they will NOT support our current announced Republican gubernatorial nominee hopeful. "She doesn't support Trump," they say. And many Trump supporters said they will stay home if she's on the ballot.
We want a Trump candidate for governor.
You see, nationally there have been so many exciting developments that have occurred over the last 30 days. In my opinion these are miracles. God answering our many prayers.
What President Trump is doing nationally with the help of Elon Musk, boldly and swiftly cleaning up decades of government waste, fraud and abuse. The RINOS are falling in line behind Trump. He's doing things that have never been done in our lifetime and it's been jaw dropping what they've found. Why?
Because strong leaders with a backbone can actually get things done for the people.
I want that for Virginia now. Don't you?
We want a Trump candidate for governor.
It just shows if you get the right person in office, things get done. If we could just find someone with the courage and hutzpah that would be willing to take on the political establishment, we could do the same thing here in Virginia.
Now that the USAID and other agencies have been exposed as corrupt slush fund for the CIA and Democrat candidates, that source of unlawful funding Democrat campaigns has dried up.
So where exactly did Abigail Spanberger get over $10 million dollars and what is she trying to hide? I think we have an idea now.
I've never been more hopeful that the right Republican can generate true excitement and get people out to vote. Let's face it. Milk toast, boring candidates don't drive people to the polls to vote.
We want a Trump candidate for governor.
President Trump's ratings have never been higher. Most Virginians approve of the job President Trump is doing more than ever in his second term in office.
Yet, our current announced Republican nominee is a Never Trumper who has really never come out and embraced our President, President Donald J Trump. She not only refused to openly and wholeheartedly support President Trump, but has spoken out against President Trump's run for a second term. Read it for yourself [here](https://byh4wqwab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011azOX-0JQPMEeAhDMKeBBsC0H6flQrCuigmrDGXtZCYup03n4XWJu1IIzK3B1Mq81xGXwR2rp3E_21YskY8Jfn5NccHiSqYWYemH7R5HKg1z-a97mziaodgMehUM-BmuSaR5dXdm6PaWiLcySAaipGGHiL2qtD0a87Y4ikKcRPhb87qmuTskDPVDCNyFggQWF-TbrvvLeC36F7T4j123bLwv50vrRbq18TDaUzjCKzTdUnPq8A5VVm4UqiHgse5Qqqoagkhfd2M=&c=0rod1UEoUe-nqKt1QAuSy1EXGsg2MPgtQTq5HknG1nUFuK6_neBRKg==&ch=ozPI7uB-LEnLlOzzsRDQHk0o9uB_d_4b1R7UA40LmbxZeWUOkJPv7g==).
Her recent response has been lukewarm at best. Even after President Trump received the Republican nomination, this gubernatorial candidate refused to come out publicly to support our Republican Nominee for President.
We want a Trump candidate for governor.
Diehard Trump supporters like me, remember that. And that's not sitting well with hundreds of thousands of Virginians who enthusiastically love and support our President.
They want a Governor who is like Trump, one who doesn't kowtow to the political establishment and actually gets things done.
Many of you have emphatically pleaded with me to run again stating, "We need a MAGA candidate for Governor, who we can vote for."
We want a Trump candidate for governor.
Many of you remember that I ran for Governor in 2020-2021, for 18 months as the pro-Trump candidate. In fact, many of you called me "Trump in Heels." I did well in the 9 candidate ranked choice convention. I finished 3rd, ahead of a popular former Speaker of the House. Many believed that had it been a primary, that I would have won.
We need "Trump in Heels" if we're going to defeat Abigail Spanberger in November.
I am that candidate.
The Republican nomination coming up this June 17th will be a primary. I was the deciding vote in the Senate to make sure it was a primary and not a convention. Thanks to my vote, you will be able to go to your local polling location between the hours of 6am and 7pm to vote.
For a candidate to run for Governor, they have to get a minimum of 10,000 signatures before Thursday, April 3 by 5pm to even get their name on the ballot. Of those signatures, 400 signatures have to come from each Congressional District. That's a heavy lift for 37 days. But I believe if the same people who volunteered to help me last time help me this time, we can do this. But we must start today.
Unfortunately, WE CANNOT COLLECT SIGNATURES ONLINE. Signatures must be witnessed in person by signing an old fashioned paper petition ballot.
So here's the deal.
If those of you who want me to run for Governor will collect the necessary signatures to get my name on the ballot by the deadline, I will run. If not, then I won't.
This requires you to do some work:
1. Print off the attached form on one sheet of paper, front and back.
2. Witness your friends, family and neighbors sign the petition form. Please make sure they actually sign the form. Please also make sure their writing is legible so that signatures can be verified.
3. Keep in mind that you can't sign your own petition form.
4. Please collect signatures by[ Congressional District.](https://byh4wqwab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011azOX-0JQPMEeAhDMKeBBsC0H6flQrCuigmrDGXtZCYup03n4XWJu1IIzK3B1Mq88Lo-jGoz4_hKN9Y4N85RTBgUKZD_I5IJ-xagN4wbTdzkYzeCzu0DFZXHn-R8mBNvqXZhtW6chs7HFr98Rx_jnB9MiOkkk0JfRF_6A1YD7pIXMmS0s5opCTMDj1WAbQ0Bw4Vb2RgJQ2c=&c=0rod1UEoUe-nqKt1QAuSy1EXGsg2MPgtQTq5HknG1nUFuK6_neBRKg==&ch=ozPI7uB-LEnLlOzzsRDQHk0o9uB_d_4b1R7UA40LmbxZeWUOkJPv7g==) One Congressional District per form.
5. Get the petition notarized.
6. Drop the petition off in person to: 2023 Church Street, Appomattox, VA 24522
7. Or mail the petition to:

Friends of Amanda Chase PO Box 250 Appomattox, VA 24522
---

| You can also use the link below to print off the petition forms. Please remember the forms must be double sided and printed front and back. You must also witness every signature and visit your local bank to have a notary sign off on your petition form before mailing.
If you have any question please email Craig at craig@chaseforva.com. If you have trouble printing the forms, we can mail you the forms.
I can't do this without your help. Print off a petition now. Don't wait. Get your immediate family to sign the petition and then get your friends at church and work to sign your petition. Time is not on our side. Less than 30 days to collect signatures. If not you, then who?

clean_body: Please read | | | | 2025 THE HONEY BADGER REPORT | | | | | | | RUNNING FOR GOVERNOR RUMORS | AMANDA CHASE | VIRGINIA'S HONEY BADGER | Dear Hello I'm absolutely humbled by the number of you who have contacted me to run for Governor. The unsolicited response has been overwhelming to the point I've decided to respond. First, I had no intentions of running for Governor this year. My thought was that we get behind our one Republican nominee who has declared, so that we don't have to waste time or money in a Republican Primary, so that we can laser focus all of our resources on defeating Democrat Governor hopeful Abigail Spanberger. In the past few days, I've learned that our only declared Republican candidate for Governor has encountered some pretty serious issues with her campaign. We now face an almost certain defeat in November, if we don't find a candidate who can manage and organize a successful campaign against Spanberger. Many in Southwest Virginia have said they will NOT support our current announced Republican gubernatorial nominee hopeful. "She doesn't support Trump," they say. And many Trump supporters said they will stay home if she's on the ballot. We want a Trump candidate for governor. You see, nationally there have been so many exciting developments that have occurred over the last 30 days. In my opinion these are miracles. God answering our many prayers. What President Trump is doing nationally with the help of Elon Musk, boldly and swiftly cleaning up decades of government waste, fraud and abuse. The RINOS are falling in line behind Trump. He's doing things that have never been done in our lifetime and it's been jaw dropping what they've found. Why? Because strong leaders with a backbone can actually get things done for the people. I want that for Virginia now. Don't you? We want a Trump candidate for governor. It just shows if you get the right person in office, things get done. If we could just find someone with the courage and hutzpah that would be willing to take on the political establishment, we could do the same thing here in Virginia. Now that the USAID and other agencies have been exposed as corrupt slush fund for the CIA and Democrat candidates, that source of unlawful funding Democrat campaigns has dried up. So where exactly did Abigail Spanberger get over $10 million dollars and what is she trying to hide? I think we have an idea now. I've never been more hopeful that the right Republican can generate true excitement and get people out to vote. Let's face it. Milk toast, boring candidates don't drive people to the polls to vote. We want a Trump candidate for governor. President Trump's ratings have never been higher. Most Virginians approve of the job President Trump is doing more than ever in his second term in office. Yet, our current announced Republican nominee is a Never Trumper who has really never come out and embraced our President, President Donald J Trump. She not only refused to openly and wholeheartedly support President Trump, but has spoken out against President Trump's run for a second term. Read it for yourself ==. Her recent response has been lukewarm at best. Even after President Trump received the Republican nomination, this gubernatorial candidate refused to come out publicly to support our Republican Nominee for President. We want a Trump candidate for governor. Diehard Trump supporters like me, remember that. And that's not sitting well with hundreds of thousands of Virginians who enthusiastically love and support our President. They want a Governor who is like Trump, one who doesn't kowtow to the political establishment and actually gets things done. Many of you have emphatically pleaded with me to run again stating, "We need a MAGA candidate for Governor, who we can vote for." We want a Trump candidate for governor. Many of you remember that I ran for Governor in 2020-2021, for 18 months as the pro-Trump candidate. In fact, many of you called me "Trump in Heels." I did well in the 9 candidate ranked choice convention. I finished 3rd, ahead of a popular former Speaker of the House. Many believed that had it been a primary, that I would have won. We need "Trump in Heels" if we're going to defeat Abigail Spanberger in November. I am that candidate. The Republican nomination coming up this June 17th will be a primary. I was the deciding vote in the Senate to make sure it was a primary and not a convention. Thanks to my vote, you will be able to go to your local polling location between the hours of 6am and 7pm to vote. For a candidate to run for Governor, they have to get a minimum of 10,000 signatures before Thursday, April 3 by 5pm to even get their name on the ballot. Of those signatures, 400 signatures have to come from each Congressional District. That's a heavy lift for 37 days. But I believe if the same people who volunteered to help me last time help me this time, we can do this. But we must start today. Unfortunately, WE CANNOT COLLECT SIGNATURES ONLINE. Signatures must be witnessed in person by signing an old fashioned paper petition ballot. So here's the deal. If those of you who want me to run for Governor will collect the necessary signatures to get my name on the ballot by the deadline, I will run. If not, then I won't. This requires you to do some work: 1. Print off the attached form on one sheet of paper, front and back. 2. Witness your friends, family and neighbors sign the petition form. Please make sure they actually sign the form. Please also make sure their writing is legible so that signatures can be verified. 3. Keep in mind that you can't sign your own petition form. 4. Please collect signatures by== One Congressional District per form. 5. Get the petition notarized. 6. Drop the petition off in person to: 2023 Church Street, Appomattox, VA 24522 7. Or mail the petition to: Friends of Amanda Chase PO Box 250 Appomattox, VA 24522 | | | | | You can also use the link below to print off the petition forms. Please remember the forms must be double sided and printed front and back. You must also witness every signature and visit your local bank to have a notary sign off on your petition form before mailing. If you have any question please email Craig at craig@chaseforva.com. If you have trouble printing the forms, we can mail you the forms. I can't do this without your help. Print off a petition now. Don't wait. Get your immediate family to sign the petition and then get your friends at church and work to sign your petition. Time is not on our side. Less than 30 days to collect signatures. # FROM THE DESK OF ALAN DERSHOWITZ
---
| | Dear Reader, In over sixty years in the legal profession, I've experienced first hand the impact of both good journalism and bad journalism -- mostly the latter -- and just how important and rare it is to get things right.

**In today 's media landscape there are far too many publications that get things wrong.** Many are more concerned with the political implications of a story than the basic facts.

**The New York Sun is different.** It's a paper that places principle over politics and people over party.

Its in-depth coverage of the legal challenges faced by President Trump serve as a case in point.

When I defended President Trump during his first impeachment, I faced an avalanche of criticism, but few papers made sufficient effort to fully appreciate the significance of the legal arguments.

The Sun's deeply knowledgeable leadership, including its editor Seth Lipsky and associate editor A.R. Hoffman are themselves students of the Constitution. It shows in their coverage, which I find to be first rate.

It will be no secret to you that I don't agree with everything that can be found in the Sun's pages, but I can say with confidence that its re-emergence is among the most important recent developments in American journalism.

I've been impressed by the Sun's growth so far, but I know it faces an uphill battle, one that I have pledged to join.

**The Sun 's success will be a gift to the American people and to the cause of truth.** But to succeed, we need you to join us. I highly encourage you to join the Sun today.

Every person matters in this effort.

Don't wait. The battle to restore American journalism starts now.

clean_body: What too many journalists get wrong For a limited time, join for just 1¢ | | | | FROM THE DESK OF ALAN DERSHOWITZ | | Dear Reader, In over sixty years in the legal profession, I've experienced first hand the impact of both good journalism and bad journalism -- mostly the latter -- and just how important and rare it is to get things right. In today 's media landscape there are far too many publications that get things wrong. Many are more concerned with the political implications of a story than the basic facts. The New York Sun is different. It's a paper that places principle over politics and people over party. Its in-depth coverage of the legal challenges faced by President Trump serve as a case in point. When I defended President Trump during his first impeachment, I faced an avalanche of criticism, but few papers made sufficient effort to fully appreciate the significance of the legal arguments. The Sun's deeply knowledgeable leadership, including its editor Seth Lipsky and associate editor A.R. Hoffman are themselves students of the Constitution. It shows in their coverage, which I find to be first rate. It will be no secret to you that I don't agree with everything that can be found in the Sun's pages, but I can say with confidence that its re-emergence is among the most important recent developments in American journalism. I've been impressed by the Sun's growth so far, but I know it faces an uphill battle, one that I have pledged to join. The Sun 's success will be a gift to the American people and to the cause of truth. But to succeed, we need you to join us. I highly encourage you to join the Sun today. Every person matters in this effort. Don't wait. Our country's current threats to care are alarming, to say the least.
The Trump administration has unleashed a storm of anti-care policies, from nominating Robert F. Kennedy, an anti-vaccination crusader, to run the Department of Human Health and Services, and pushing massive budget cuts to critical health care programs like Medicaid.
These actions are extremely damaging to our communities, especially Black domestic workers.
But throughout history, Black women have been the caregivers that **built this nation,** despite centuries of exploitation. In the face of today’s threats to care, Black women are **stepping up AGAIN.**

I recently mustered the courage to read, "The Cruel Kids' Table," which not surprisingly made it onto the cover of _New York Magazine_ the days after Trump's Inauguration. In addition to cropping black people out of the photo that appeared on the cover, the piece reads like it was written by the bitter bohemian who was not only the last pick on the kickball team but also too dumb to make it into the spelling bee or the debate team.
If you can make it through this whopper of an opening sentence, I will consider you both stunning AND brave: "It's Monday, January 20, the first night of Donald Trump's second presidency, and just a couple blocks from the Capitol building that his now-pardoned MAGA army swarmed four years and 14 days ago, there is, and there has been for the past several nights in restaurants, hotel ballrooms, and lobbying offices, a party for people who have never been happier about the direction in which this country is heading."
January 6 conflation aside (I should know I was actually there), the second graph contained the only material observation in a pile of half-truths passed off as journalism, "This party is at Butterworth's, a new dimly lit bistro that has become a hot spot for the right."
I decided to go to Butterworth's and see if there were actually any black people since they were conveniently absent from the article. While I have neither the credentials nor the self-hatred to write for a publication as disreputable as NY Mag, I do have enough honesty to tell the truth based on my observations: Minorities like Donald Trump too!
CJ Pearson, the black American who hosted the Butterworth's event covered in the piece, was left out of the version that made it to print.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eae4d57a-4fcf-44ed-a7b0-d4e107632a5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/da362298-20e2-429f-a88f-2d1b2cb46589?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
CJ hosted yet another event at Butterworth's in the midst of this year's Conservative Political Action Committee (CPAC). I caught up with CJ in the back of Butterworth's and he had some choice words for the publication, "I hosted the entire board to organize the entire party. But what _New York Magazine_ would have you to believe is that there we're some KKK kumbayah, some white supremacists just, I don't know, like, it was insane. But what they left out is the fact that many black people were in attendance. I mean, black congressmen, black activists, black influencers, black rappers, black athletes. And the entire party was organized by a black man. But what you'll see is that the MAGA movement is as diverse as it's ever been before, and the media doesn't want to acknowledge that."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ba5455d3-57b7-4a6f-a88e-cbfc6a65f85d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Tim Scott, a Trump supporter and the longest-serving black American in the United States Senate, stepped onto the stage at the front of the event space in the restaurant, "it is powerful to see the energy in this room and around the country for what you all made possible... And I mean the ones in this room that made Donald Trump President."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1cff4481-ea62-4665-9d46-f432c7caacb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I talked with the bartender who worked at the joint since it opened in 2024, and he told me that he did not experience the cruelty that _New York Magazine_ suggested was the norm among those who frequent this place, "At the end of the day, everyone is respectful and treats us with love."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5026bf95-a0fb-4c2a-829f-bd857a0ef8bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Olivia Rondeau, a mixed-race reporter, had a similar take, "I'm good friends with CJ Pearson who is the person who put on that event, and obviously there are minorities here, obviously there are multiethnic people here. And I just think that it's so fake and false news that we're portrayed as white supremacists or something."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/93a71818-4fb0-47b2-8520-5e6778f548d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I also spoke with Raheem Kassem, one of the owners of the restaurant, and he emphasized that all are welcome at Butterworth's, regardless of how they look or how they vote. "We do fantastic French food, extraordinarily good cocktails, and cater to anyone regardless of their placement on the political spectrum. We're less interested in what color hats people are wearing (please don't wear ANY hats during dinner service) and more interested in elevating their palates and sending them home full and happy and naughtily sozzled. Anyone who's cool with that is welcome."
The energy in the room when I visited discernibly less "cruel" and more diverse than what was described in the pages of _New York Magazine_. It was clear from the copy that the reporter sought and then highlighted the most reprehensible comments they could find: "Outside on the sidewalk, two tuxedoed men smoking Marlboros are trying to remember what exactly the president said that morning. _Are we entering a New Dawn? A New Era? Wait, was it Golden Era? Golden Dawn?_ They erupt into laughter. 'It's a little bit Hitlerian,' one concludes."

# **The World 's Most Well-Connected Bankers Are RUSHING To Accumulate Physical Gold**
